jurisdiction.name: Tunisia
jurisdiction.overview: Tunisia has no AI-specific law or published national AI strategy; AI is governed through the 2004 personal data protection law, a pending data protection bill, and sector guidance for higher education.

narrative.summary: Tunisia has no AI-specific law and no officially published national AI strategy: a 2018 strategy process led by the research ministry never produced a published text, and a National AI Strategy 2026-2030 prepared by the Ministry of Communication Technologies was presented to a ministerial council in 2026 but its text has not been released. Binding rules that reach AI come from Organic Law 2004-63 on personal data protection, supervised by the INPDP. A replacement data protection bill (proposal 095/2025), under examination by parliament's Rights and Freedoms Committee, would add a right to object to decisions based solely on automated processing and profiling, privacy by design and periodic risk analysis. The most concrete published AI guidance is sectoral: the Université Virtuelle de Tunis has issued a strategic action plan for AI in higher education and research (2025) and a charter on good use of AI, including generative AI, in Tunisian universities (December 2025). Cybersecurity is regulated by Decree-Law 2023-17 and the ANCS, but neither the decree-law nor the ANCS strategies contain AI-specific requirements.
lead_institutions: Instance Nationale de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (INPDP)
Assembly of the Representatives of the People (ARP)
Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research / Université Virtuelle de Tunis
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 6 October 2026. The data protection law was read from an official government copy because the data protection authority's website could not be reached and the official journal cannot be linked directly. The 2025 data protection bill was checked page by page from Parliament's scan. Cybersecurity laws and strategies, the central bank's fintech sandbox and the Startup Act were reviewed and contain no AI-specific provisions. The university AI documents are recorded as sector guidance from a public university. Tunisia's party status under Convention 108 is to be added to the regional layer.

French text read from the copy hosted by the Institut National de la Statistique; inpdp.tn refused automated connections.
instruments.summary: Tunisia's framework data protection law (105 articles). It applies to automated and non-automated processing of personal data by natural and legal persons, requires processing to respect transparency, fairness and human dignity, makes most processing subject to prior declaration or authorisation by the INPDP (which it establishes), and sets data-subject rights of access, rectification and objection, rules on sensitive data, transfers abroad and criminal penalties. It governs personal data used to train or run AI systems but contains no AI-specific provisions.

instruments.summary: Sector roadmap for AI in Tunisian higher education and research, built with the country's universities. It sets six strategic objectives: training academics in AI, responsible AI research and innovation, AI tools for teaching and learning, AI-enabled digital transformation of universities, an ethical, inclusive and responsible approach to AI (including an ethics charter), and AI governance in the sector (a national steering body), with a five-year operational plan. It guides universities and is not binding.

instruments.current_status: Members' bill (initiated by a group of MPs, Al-Ahrar bloc) filed 14 July 2025 and referred on 16 July 2025 to the Rights and Freedoms Committee; committee hearings held February–June 2026 (incl. Presidency of the Government, INPDP and Ministry of Health). First reading in committee; not adopted as of 2026-10-06. Text is a scanned PDF (no text layer); provisions checked by reading page images.
instruments.summary: Parliamentary bill that would replace Organic Law 2004-63 with a new personal data protection regime overseen by a Personal Data Protection Authority. It defines biometric, genetic and health data and "profiling" (any automated processing used to evaluate personal aspects of an individual), gives data subjects a right to object including to decisions based solely on automated processing or profiling (Art. 29), and requires controllers to build data protection into system design (Art. 42) and to carry out periodic risk analyses of processing (Art. 44). It is a draft with no legal effect.

instruments.current_status: Consolidated Version 2 dated 19 December 2025, an initiative of the Université Virtuelle de Tunis drawn up with university partners after the 4 December 2025 day "La stratégie de l'IA dans l'ES en action". Framed within the general teaching charter and Ministry of Higher Education policies; no ministerial adoption act found.
instruments.summary: Charter for teachers, students, researchers and administration in Tunisian higher education on responsible use of AI, including generative and agentic AI. It sets principles of transparency and declaration of AI use, final human responsibility, awareness of algorithmic bias, equity and accessibility, and environmental impact, followed by specific rules for teachers (clear instructions, adapted assessment, explainability) and students (AI as an assistant, not a substitute for intellectual effort). It is guidance and carries no sanctions of its own.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Searched official sources (MTC, Presidency of the Government, ARP, ANCS, INPDP, BCT, INNORPI, HAICOP/marchespublics.gov.tn, INTT, ministries of health and higher education) in Arabic, French and English: no AI-specific law, published national AI strategy, AI governance body founding act, public-sector or procurement AI rules, AI security guidance, transparency rules, AI standards adoption, AI sandbox, government AI index or AI treaty ratification found as of 2026-10-06. The 2026-2030 national AI strategy, 2018 strategy process and BCT generative-AI charter are recorded as leads. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-06. Organic Law 2004-63 read from the copy hosted by the Institut National de la Statistique (inpdp.tn and inpdp.nat.tn refused automated connections; iort.gov.tn/JORT is a WinDev application that cannot be deep-linked; pist.tn reset connections). legislation-securite.tn was used only for discovery (non-governmental database), never as a source. The ARP bill 095/2025 PDF is a scan without a text layer; its provisions were checked from page images. Excluded after reading: Decree-Law 2023-17 on cybersecurity (JORT n°26, 11 March 2023) and the ANCS National Cybersecurity Strategy 2020-2025 and 2026-2030 consultation (May 2025) - general cyber instruments without AI-specific provisions; ANCS/Presidency Circular No. 5 of 2026 (2 Sept 2026) on securing public digital systems - not AI; BCT Regulatory Sandbox access guide (January 2020) - fintech sandbox, not AI-specific; Tunisie Digitale 2020 plan - no AI pillar; Startup Act (Law 2018-20) - not AI-specific; Decree 2026-1 amending Decree-Law 2022-54 on cybercrime - not AI; SNJT journalism AI charter (2026) - trade union, not an official body. The anpr.tn 2018 page is only a workshop announcement. The UVT documents are publications of a public university acting for the higher-education sector, not ministerial acts; recorded as sectoral guidance. Convention 108 (Tunisia a party since 2017) is not in data/regional/COE.json; COE AI Framework Convention: Tunisia not a signatory as far as found. AU Continental AI Strategy and UNESCO Recommendation apply via regional files.
